--src: Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
@[deprecated mul_pos (since := "2024-08-15")]
protected theorem mul_pos {a b : ℝ} : 0 < a → 0 < b → 0 < a * b := by
  induction' a using Real.ind_mk with a
  induction' b using Real.ind_mk with b
  simpa only [mk_lt, mk_pos, ← mk_mul] using CauSeq.mul_pos

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
lemma strictAnti_rpow_of_base_lt_one {b : ℝ} (hb₀ : 0 < b) (hb₁ : b < 1) :
    StrictAnti (b ^ · : ℝ → ℝ) := by
  simp_rw [Real.rpow_def_of_pos hb₀]
  exact exp_strictMono.comp_strictAnti <| StrictMono.const_mul_of_neg strictMono_id
      <| Real.log_neg hb₀ hb₁

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.SpecificFunctions.Basic
/-- `Real.exp` is convex on the whole real line. -/
theorem convexOn_exp : ConvexOn ℝ univ exp :=
  strictConvexOn_exp.convexOn

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
lemma strictMono_rpow_of_base_gt_one {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 < b) :
    StrictMono (b ^ · : ℝ → ℝ) := by
  simp_rw [Real.rpow_def_of_pos (zero_lt_one.trans hb)]
  exact exp_strictMono.comp <| StrictMono.const_mul strictMono_id <| Real.log_pos hb

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Asymptotics
/-- `exp (-a * x) = o(x ^ s)` as `x → ∞`, for any positive `a` and real `s`. -/
theorem isLittleO_exp_neg_mul_rpow_atTop {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (b : ℝ) :
    IsLittleO atTop (fun x : ℝ => exp (-a * x)) fun x : ℝ => x ^ b := by
  apply isLittleO_of_tendsto'
  · refine (eventually_gt_atTop 0).mono fun t ht h => ?_
    rw [rpow_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg ht.le] at h
    exact (ht.ne' h.1).elim
  · refine (tendsto_exp_mul_div_rpow_atTop (-b) a ha).inv_tendsto_atTop.congr' ?_
    refine (eventually_ge_atTop 0).mono fun t ht => ?_
    field_simp [Real.exp_neg, rpow_neg ht]

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
@[bound]
theorem rpow_pos_of_pos {x : ℝ} (hx : 0 < x) (y : ℝ) : 0 < x ^ y := by
  rw [rpow_def_of_pos hx]; apply exp_pos

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Real
lemma monotone_rpow_of_base_ge_one {b : ℝ} (hb : 1 ≤ b) :
    Monotone (b ^ · : ℝ → ℝ) := by
  rcases lt_or_eq_of_le hb with hb | rfl
  case inl => exact (strictMono_rpow_of_base_gt_one hb).monotone
  case inr => intro _ _ _; simp

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Integrals
@[simp]
theorem integral_inv_of_pos (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : ∫ x in a..b, x⁻¹ = log (b / a) :=
  integral_inv <| not_mem_uIcc_of_lt ha hb

--src: Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Log.Base
theorem logb_rpow_eq_mul_logb_of_pos (hx : 0 < x) : logb b (x ^ y) = y * logb b x := by
  rw [logb, log_rpow hx, logb, mul_div_assoc]

theorem ConvexOn_rpow_left (b : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun (x : ℝ) => b ^ x) := by
  have : (fun x => b ^ x) = (Real.exp ∘ (Real.log b * ·)) := by
    ext x
    simp only [comp_apply]
    rw [<-Real.rpow_def_of_pos hb]
  rw [this]
  exact ConvexOn.comp_linearMap convexOn_exp (LinearMap.mul ℝ ℝ (Real.log b))

C1_dependencies.name: Real.log
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The real logarithm function, equal to the inverse of the exponential for `x > 0`,
to `log |x|` for `x < 0`, and to `0` for `0`. We use this unconventional extension to
`(-∞, 0]` as it gives the formula `log (x * y) = log x + log y` for all nonzero `x` and `y`, and
the derivative of `log` is `1/x` away from `0`. -/
@[pp_nodot]
noncomputable def log (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  if hx : x = 0 then 0 else expOrderIso.symm ⟨|x|, abs_pos.2 hx⟩

C1_dependencies.name: LinearMap.mul
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The multiplication in a non-unital non-associative algebra is a bilinear map.

A weaker version of this for semirings exists as `AddMonoidHom.mul`. -/
@[simps!]
def mul : A →ₗ[R] A →ₗ[R] A :=
  LinearMap.mk₂ R (· * ·) add_mul smul_mul_assoc mul_add mul_smul_comm

C1_dependencies.name: ConvexOn.comp_linearMap
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- If `g` is convex on `s`, so is `(f ∘ g)` on `f ⁻¹' s` for a linear `f`. -/
theorem ConvexOn.comp_linearMap {f : F → β} {s : Set F} (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (g : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) :
    ConvexOn 𝕜 (g ⁻¹' s) (f ∘ g) :=
  ⟨hf.1.linear_preimage _, fun x hx y hy a b ha hb hab =>
    calc
      f (g (a • x + b • y)) = f (a • g x + b • g y) := by rw [g.map_add, g.map_smul, g.map_smul]
      _ ≤ a • f (g x) + b • f (g y) := hf.2 hx hy ha hb hab⟩
C1_dependencies.compilationAlias:
/-- If `g` is convex on `s`, so is `(f ∘ g)` on `f ⁻¹' s` for a linear `f`. -/
theorem ConvexOn.comp_linearMap {f : F → β} {s : Set F} (hf : ConvexOn 𝕜 s f) (g : E →ₗ[𝕜] F) :
    ConvexOn 𝕜 (g ⁻¹' s) (f ∘ g) :=
  ⟨hf.1.linear_preimage _, fun x hx y hy a b ha hb hab =>
    calc
      f (g (a • x + b • y)) = f (a • g x + b • g y) := by rw [g.map_add, g.map_smul, g.map_smul]
      _ ≤ a • f (g x) + b • f (g y) := hf.2 hx hy ha hb hab⟩

C1_dependencies.name: Set.univ
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- The universal set on a type `α` is the set containing all elements of `α`.

This is conceptually the "same as" `α` (in set theory, it is actually the same), but type theory
makes the distinction that `α` is a type while `Set.univ` is a term of type `Set α`. `Set.univ` can
itself be coerced to a type `↥Set.univ` which is in bijection with (but distinct from) `α`. -/
def univ : Set α := {_a | True}

def univ : Set α := {_a | True}

C1_dependencies.name: ConvexOn
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- Convexity of functions -/
def ConvexOn : Prop :=
  Convex 𝕜 s ∧ ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → ∀ ⦃a b : 𝕜⦄, 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → a + b = 1 →
    f (a • x + b • y) ≤ a • f x + b • f y
